title: Simulating the Dicke Model on Qubit-Based and hybrid Qubit-Boson-Based Quantum Computers
authors: Aravind P. Babu, Seongjin Ahn, Jing Sun, Augustas G. Landsbergis, Andrey S. Moskalenko, Marko J. Rančić
abstract: The Dicke model provides a fundamental description of collective light-matter interactions and has long served as a testbed for exploring a wide range of physical phenomena in quantum optics and condensed matter physics. In this work, we develop a variational framework for investigating the finite-size Dicke model on both fully qubit-based (digital) and hybrid qubit boson based (digital-analogue) quantum computing platforms. We show that the resulting model reproduces the characteristic critical behavior of the Dicke model in the appropriate large-spin limit while remaining suitable for implementation on both classical emulators of quantum computers and actual trapped ion quantum computers, albeit in the case of latter somewhat limited by noise. Finally, we introduce a complementary hybrid qubit-bosonic variational ansatz that directly exploits the bosonic degree of freedom to reduce quantum resources and discuss its potential implementation on hybrid quantum hardware. Our results establish a scalable, symmetry-aware framework for variational quantum simulations of collective light-matter systems and provide a pathway toward efficient simulations of more general spin-boson models on near-term quantum devices.
summary: The paper presents a variational framework to simulate the Dicke model—a key system in quantum optics—on current and future quantum computers. It develops specialized ansätze for both purely qubit-based and hybrid qubit-boson platforms, showing that these methods can accurately capture critical phase transitions. This establishes a scalable methodology for simulating complex light-matter interactions on near-term devices.
main_problem: Developing a variational framework to simulate the finite-size Dicke model on both fully qubit-based (digital) and hybrid qubit-boson based quantum computing platforms.
main_result: The developed framework successfully reproduces the characteristic critical behavior of the Dicke model in the large-spin limit, offering a scalable path for simulating collective light-matter systems.
method: Variational Quantum Algorithms (VQAs), specifically VQE, are employed. The bosonic mode is mapped to qubits via Holstein-Primakoff transformation or treated directly using hybrid ansätze.
model_or_system: The Dicke model describes collective light-matter interactions and can be generalized to inhomogeneous forms. It is studied on quantum computing platforms ranging from fully qubit-encoded systems to hybrid qubit-boson architectures.
key_observables: Average photon number ($\langle a^\dagger a angle / N$), critical behavior, and precursors of the superradiant phase transition.
important_parameters: Coupling strength ($\lambda/\lambda_c$), system size ($N$), and bosonic excitation limit ($M=2s$).
main_assumptions: The approach assumes that symmetry-preserving ansätze can be constructed, though limitations exist for $N>4$ in achieving perfect symmetry preparation.
figures_summary: Figure 1(b) shows the convergence of the spin-Dicke model's behavior towards the full Dicke model as the bosonic representation size ($M$) increases.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the variational framework, details the mapping from the continuous boson mode to qubits (spin-Dicke model), develops symmetry-aware ansätze for both fully digital and hybrid representations, and analyzes the resulting critical behavior.
why_interesting: This work directly bridges fundamental quantum optics models (Dicke) with near-term quantum hardware constraints by proposing resource-efficient simulation techniques.
